text.p: Bulgaria's 1996 Gross Domestic Product (GDP) slumped by ten percent compared to a 2.5 percent growth in 1995, the National Statiscs Institute (NSI) said on Thursday.
The GDP stood at 1.7 trillion levs in current prices in 1996 compared to 852 billion levs in 1995.

"The figures show that all macroeconomic indicators for the past year have negative values, this shows that the country is in a total economic crisis," NSI directo Zahari Karamfilov told a news conference.
Industrial output fell by 1.1 percent last year and agricultural output fell by 13.1 percent, NSI figures show. Construction has shrunk by 20 percent.
These dire statistics are a result of a lack of consistent restructuring policy and delayed privatisation, said Karamfilov.
Local businessmen, polled by the NSI, said they would be forced to reduce production further to meet shrinking demand and lay off personnel.
The private sector accounted for about one third of last year's GDP, the NSI said.
